dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product frames its pages the same way everywhere: a header, its navigation, the content, sometimes an aside, a footer. It shows that frame in a wide window and in a narrow one, gives its reading pages a limited width and its working pages all of it, and lets a keyboard pass the frame in one step.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything an app shell reads: the frame's fill and the text color it hands down; the two window widths that part the three window classes (compact, medium, expanded); the gutter of each class; the main region's readable width and its space above and below; the aside's width, inset and its distance from the main content when stacked; the footer's space above and below; how touching regions are parted and the hairline that parts them; and the box the skip link is shown in.
rules: The shell places regions and draws none of their content. The header is an app bar, the navigation a navigation drawer, the aside the product's content or a side sheet, the bottom bar a navigation bar: each keeps its own tokens.

breakpoint.medium and breakpoint.expanded are widths of the window, not sizes of anything drawn. They alias the system's window classes (sys.breakpoint), as a responsive navigation drawer's do; never set one without the other, and set the drawer's with them.
A gutter is the distance between the frame and the content of the main region, of a stacked aside and of the footer. One per window class; nothing else in the shell changes size with the class.
main.max-width limits what is read. A page that is worked in (a table, an editor) sets mainWidth to full instead of raising the token.
separation follows the system's choice; set it here only to part this one component differently.
The shell has no states, no motion and no elevation of its own. The skip link's box is the one raised thing, and only while the link has keyboard focus.
There is no token for the header's height, the navigation's width or the footer's layout: they belong to what the product puts there.

color.$description: The frame's fill: what shows wherever no region draws a fill of its own, and under the system insets.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product sets its pages on its surface color and may set an app's frame on a dimmer one, so that the panes in it read as raised.

color.$description: The text color the frame hands to what it holds, as the inherited foreground. Prose and plain content bring none of their own.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: Whatever the frame's fill is, text placed straight on it must be readable on it; the pair is set together.

One product has one set of window classes: the width from which its navigation leaves the layout and the width from which there is room for a third column are the same on every page, and it sets them where they suit its own content.

medium.$description: The window width from which the class is medium. Below it the window is compact: one column, the navigation over the content, a navigation bar at the bottom where the product gives one.

expanded.$description: The window width from which the class is expanded: the navigation and the aside stand beside the main content.

gutter.$description: The inset of the main region's content, of a stacked aside and of the footer's content from the start and the end of their region, per window class.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product keeps its content closer to the edge of a phone than to the edge of a desktop window: a narrow window has no width to spend on margins, and a wide one looks crowded without them.

max-width.$description: The greatest width of the main region's content while mainWidth is contained: the prose's measure at the default text size with room for the blocks that are wider than text (a table, a code block, a figure).

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product limits the width of what is read, whatever the window, and a product with denser or larger text sets the limit to suit it.

padding-block.$description: Space above and below the main region's content, and above and below the content of an aside that stands beside it, so that their first lines are level.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product decides how far its content starts below its header and how much room it leaves before the footer.

One product shows supporting content beside its main content in a wide window, in a column narrow enough to leave the main content its width, and stacks the two, a clear step apart, where there is no room.

width.$description: The width of the aside beside the main content, its insets included, where what it holds has no width of its own. The navigation drawer's width in the default system, so that the frame is even on both sides.

padding-inline.$description: Inset of the aside's content from the start and the end of its column while it stands beside the main content.

gap.$description: Distance between the main content and an aside stacked above or below it. A dividing line, where one is drawn, runs in its middle.

padding-block.$description: Space above and below the footer's content.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product sets its footer apart from the end of the content by space, and how much is its own choice.

separation.$description: How regions that touch are told apart. divider: a line of outline.width in outline.color above the footer, at the start edge of an aside beside the main content, and between the main content and a stacked aside. gap: no line, the same spaces. Follows the system's choice; the shell's separation prop overrides it (APS-18). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product rules its menus and joined buttons with a line and still parts the regions of its page by space alone, or the other way round: a line across a whole page is not the same decision as a line inside a control, so the frame must be able to leave the system's choice.
One product may draw the lines of its page frame lighter or heavier than the dividers inside its components, as it may an app bar's or a drawer's edge.

color.$description: The color of the lines the shell draws between regions: the system's one hairline.

width.$description: The thickness of those lines, and of the edge the skip link's box gains in a forced-colors mode.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows its skip link, when the keyboard reaches it, in a box that stands out from the header it covers, in the product's own shape and at the product's own distance from the corner.

color.$description: The fill of the box the focused skip link is shown in: a raised surface, on which a standard Link is readable.

elevation.$description: How far the box is raised: above a sticky header and everything else in the frame.

shape.$description: The box's corners: the corner of a control.

padding-inline.$description: Inset of the link from the start and the end of the box.

padding-block.$description: Inset of the link from the top and the bottom of the box: with one line of the label's text style the box reaches the pointer target's height.

offset.$description: Distance of the box from the top and the start edges of the window, inside the system insets.

typescale.$description: The text style of the skip link in its box. Its color, underline and focus ring are the Link's own.
